Ellen — thanks for the sample, looks useful. I ran a quick pass and attached our preflight template (xls) that captures the fields we need to size reserved capacity. Quick notes from the CSV:

- Peak concurrency appears concentrated in a 40-minute window daily (~210 concurrent sessions in sample).
- Median prompt length ~60 tokens; median response ~220 tokens. That mix favors occupancy rather than per-token compute for short prompts, but token cost still matters for overall monthly billing.
- There are short bursts (10–15m) of highly concurrent agent-assist calls with low response length but high arrival rate.

Immediate asks for you to fill into the template so we can produce a conservative sizing:
1) Expected 99th-percentile concurrency target during pilot (if different from sample).
2) SLA: p95 latency target for chat and p99 tail for autocomplete requests.
3) Any planned background batching/async jobs that will also hit the pool (embeddings, nightly batches).
4) Tolerance for fallback (can we route to a lower-capacity variant during bursts?).

I'll loop Karthik for a quick fleet sketch once we have those fields. Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sizing sync Wednesday 11/1 — does that work for your team?

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_preflight_template.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Adding a few technical clarifications from the sizing playbook:

- Token mixture matters for KV cache occupancy: for agent-assist flows where user prompt is short but model responses are long, we recommend planning for a 1.8x KV cache factor (affects memory and slot usage).
- If HelioSoft plans to use streaming frequently, per-connection GPU occupancy will increase (more persistent sockets). Please specify percent of calls expected to stream vs non-streaming.
- For compute estimates, share model family you expect to pin (e.g., open-llama-34b-quant or rwkv-like models) — different kernels and quant choices change throughput 20–40%.

Tentative fleet sketch we can refine in the sync:
- Month-1 conservative: 8 x A100-style GPUs (reserved) with 2:1 oversubscription for latency-sensitive traffic, with burst pool of 2 GPUs on dedicated burst capacity.
- Canary & fallback: route to a smaller quantized variant in the same region to preserve latency if committed slots saturate.

I'll prepare a one-slide capacity sketch and a short table mapping prompt/response tiers to GPU slot counts for Wednesday.

—Marissa
Senior Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@heliosoft.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-01T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry — traffic roster & token mix (HelioSoft)

Ellen / team — thanks for moving quickly. I've sketched a first-pass capacity outline based on the sample + Priyom/Marissa notes. Key assumptions listed below; we'll lock numbers after your answers to Priyom's template fields.

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: 34B quantized family (throughput baseline: ~25 tokens/sec per GPU for mixed prompt/response workloads).
- Peak concurrent sessions to serve with p95 <= 350ms: 220 (from sample); target safety margin: 1.25x -> plan for 275 concurrent sessions on reserve.
- Average session token consumption per call: 280 tokens (60 prompt + 220 response).

Preliminary sizing (Month-1 pilot, conservative):
- Reserved pool: 10 GPUs (A100-equivalent); expected sustained occupancy ~70% at peak with 2:1 oversubscription.
- Burst buffer: 3 GPUs available for 30-minute surge windows (auto-add via burst policy).
- KV cache memory estimate: provision for 0.9 GB/session peak (includes model KV + session state) — impacts slot count if sessions have long history.

Operational asks for HelioSoft before we finalize:
- Confirm percent streaming vs standard response (est. 12% streaming increases persistent sockets and may add ~20% GPU memory headroom).
- Provide any SLA exceptions for regional failover during cloud maintenance windows.
- Sample of 7-day token breakdown (hourly) if possible — the single-day CSV is helpful but week-level shape reduces risk for overcommit.

If that looks reasonable, let's take the 30-minute sync at 14:00 PST today to go through the template and I'll bring a short cost vs latency tradeoff table.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Pre-Sales Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference
